{
  "project_id": "P-UGA-IntegratedWaterMgmtDev",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Regional instability from the South Sudan conflict could increase refugee inflows, overwhelming water and sanitation services and public finances.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Strengthen coordination with UNHCR and OPM, develop contingency funding, and prioritize flexible service delivery models for host communities.",
      "evidence": "Strategic Context – A. County Context: \"The most critical risk to this outlook is regional instability, particularly from the ongoing conflict in South Sudan... could affect export earnings and place an excessive amount of pressure on Uganda’s public services and natural resources.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Delays and cost overruns in construction due to incomplete designs, geotechnical studies, and specification gaps.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Finalize detailed designs and geotechnical studies before tender, use robust procurement specifications, and monitor progress with a contract management plan.",
      "evidence": "Key issues and risks – Procurement: \"delayed construction and underestimation of the cost of works; incomplete needs assessments and inadequate attention to geotechnical studies leading to design changes/variations during implementation.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Limited procurement capacity and inexperience with IDA procurement regulations may cause processing delays and non‑compliance.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Recruit a procurement specialist and assistant, provide intensive training on World Bank Procurement Regulations, and assign a dedicated procurement unit for the project.",
      "evidence": "Procurement capacity risk assessment – \"PDU staff have no experience in using World Bank Procurement Regulations and Procedures and have a heavy workload; MWE staff have no experience with IDA‑funded procurement.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Domestic contractors may lack capacity to execute complex water‑infrastructure works, leading to reliance on international firms and possible delays.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Conduct market sounding, encourage joint ventures and sub‑contracts with experienced foreign firms, and provide capacity‑building workshops for local contractors.",
      "evidence": "Key issues and risks – Procurement: \"limited capacity of domestic contractors to conduct projects of this nature, complexity, and scope; most contracts will be done by international firms.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Climate change (extreme temperature, intense precipitation, floods) may damage water‑source infrastructure and reduce service reliability.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Integrate climate‑resilient design, implement catchment protection (reforestation, buffer zones), and include flood‑risk assessments in all engineering studies.",
      "evidence": "Technical – Climate screening: \"identified risks included extreme temperature... increase in the annual variability of precipitation and extreme precipitation events, which in turn are likely to cause floods... Project includes source protection measures such as restoration of riverine vegetation, reforestation, and buffer zone protection.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Gender‑based violence (GBV) risk arising from long distances women and girls travel to fetch water.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement gender‑sensitive infrastructure (closer standpipes, gender‑segregated facilities), conduct GBV prevention training, and integrate GBV safeguards in ESMPs.",
      "evidence": "Gender Analysis – \"Women and girls bear the heaviest burden for water collection. Long walks to water sources trigger serious social consequences, including GBV, such as sexual assaults of women and girls... The Project will address these impacts... construct infrastructure to improve accessibility and include GBV prevention.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Labor influx associated with construction may increase social tensions and GBV incidents in host communities.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Develop a Labor Influx Management Plan, prioritize local hiring, enforce a code of conduct, and provide community sensitization on gender and safety.",
      "evidence": "Labor influx – \"The proposed Project will apply utmost due diligence in the management and monitoring of labor influx to minimize any potential GBV... include sourcing local workforce, code of conduct, mandatory training on legal conduct and GBV prevention.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Umbrella Water Authorities (UWAs) may not generate sufficient revenue to fund capital investments, risking service continuity.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Introduce full cost‑recovery tariffs with a 25 % margin, establish a revolving financing facility, and seek supplemental donor financing for capital works.",
      "evidence": "Umbrella model – \"UWAs can cover their routine O&M costs, they do not generate enough revenue to cover their capital investments... GoU has been piloting a Revolving Financing Facility with the UWAs as well as securing external financing from donors.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "National Water and Sewerage Corporation (NWSC) may be overstretched by the rapid transfer of many small‑town schemes, affecting operational performance.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Phase the transfer of responsibilities, provide targeted capacity‑building for NWSC staff, and use professionalisation contracts with private firms for O&M support.",
      "evidence": "Umbrella approach – \"NWSC does not have capacity to assume management of all Uganda’s 1,000 plus small‑to‑medium‑size schemes... GoU decided on the umbrella approach to manage this challenge.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "The Project module of the Integrated Financial Management System (IFMS) is not operational, risking inaccurate financial reporting and delays in disbursement.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Fully operationalize the IFMS project module before implementation, supplement with manual reconciliations, and conduct regular internal audits.",
      "evidence": "Financial Management – \"The main accounts of the MWE are computerized with Integrated Financial Management Systems (IFMS). However, this system is currently only operational for government funds as the project module is not yet fully operational. As a result, project financial reports cannot be generated directly from the IFMS.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Delay in finalizing the subsidiary agreement between the Ministry of Finance and NWSC could postpone fund release.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Prioritize legal review and signing of the subsidiary agreement within six months of effectiveness, with oversight from the Project Support Team.",
      "evidence": "Legal Covenants – \"Subsidiary Agreement: To facilitate the carrying out of the NWSC’s Respective Part of the Project, the Recipient shall make available part of the proceeds of the Financing... under a subsidiary agreement...\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Environmental risks from handling asbestos‑cement pipes and potential violation of minimum environmental flows could cause regulatory non‑compliance.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Include AC handling procedures in ESMP, monitor EF at intake points, and enforce compliance with OP/BP 4.01 and 4.37 safeguards.",
      "evidence": "Environmental and Social – \"The ESMP includes management measures for the removal, packaging, transportation and disposal of existing asbestos waste... Minimum environmental flow (EF) will be maintained through augmentation of the source.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "High non‑revenue water (NRW) levels (≈29 %) may erode cost‑recovery ratios and financial viability of schemes.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement NRW reduction programmes, expand metering, and enforce leak detection and repair protocols.",
      "evidence": "Performance of UWAs – \"NRW at 29 percent, and metering rates at 80 percent... The UWAs can cover their routine O&M costs, but many schemes need NRW reduction to improve financial sustainability.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Risk of procurement fraud or corruption could lead to loss of funds and reputational damage.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Apply World Bank anti‑corruption guidelines, use two‑envelope bidding for high‑value contracts, and conduct regular procurement supervision missions.",
      "evidence": "Procurement – \"The Project will be conducted in accordance with the World Bank’s ‘Procurement Regulations… and Guidelines on Preventing and Combating Fraud and Corruption in Projects…\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Disbursement delays may occur if interim financial reports (IFRs) are not submitted on time or are inaccurate.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish a clear reporting calendar, assign dedicated staff for IFR preparation, and implement a tracking system for report submission.",
      "evidence": "Disbursements – \"The World Bank will make advance disbursements… based on quarterly IFRs submitted no later than 45 days after the end of each calendar quarter.\""
    }
  ]
}
